name: Wedding Cake House (George W. Bourne House)

dates.note: The Library's item record prints '1826- 1829 Initial Construction' and '1855 Subsequent Work', and its significance note says 'The conventional late Federal style brick house was built in 1826 for George W. Bourne, a shipbuilder at a Kennebunk River shipyard. In 1855, Bourne designed and added the elaborate Gothic Revival trim.' The Wikipedia infobox instead prints 'Construction started 1825, 1852' and 'Completed 1825, 1856', and the article says the barn burned in 1852 and was rebuilt in the Gothic manner. Both are recorded; neither is resolved. The node's exemplar carries 1855, the date of the Gothic work, because that is the event the style node is about.

note: Tranche 2, Gothic Revival and picturesque villa cluster, 5 Sep 2026. Added to carpenter-gothic as the sharpest specimen of that node's own thesis -- the survey records a brick Federal main block and puts every Gothic thing on the outer inch of it. The data page was extracted twice with different queries; the second pass returned the cover, the porch and the decorative trim, which the first did not. The Library's item record prints this in its `rights_information` field; an internal run of spaces in the JSON has been collapsed to one and nothing else was changed. It is the boilerplate the Library prints on every HABS item alike and no licence is read out of it.
